exposure: fetal heart rate (FHR) decelerations (late, combined, prolonged, variable, absent variability within decelerations)
FHR below baseline ≥ 50% of the time
outcome: neonatal acidemia (defined by cord pH < 7.10 after 1st stage C-section or pH < 7.05 after vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 365 cases with neonatal acidemia (cord pH < 7.10 after 1st stage C-section or pH < 7.05 after vaginal delivery) and 730 controls with cord pH ≥ 7.15, all born at >34+0 weeks after induced or spontaneous labour.
finding: Late, prolonged, and combined fetal heart rate decelerations, along with FHR being below baseline for a significant duration, are strongly associated with an increased risk of neonatal acidemia.
